Author: Ajay Bhanot
Bench: Ajay Bhanot
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:AHC:65416 Court No. - 64 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 745 of 2024 Applicant :- Kala Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Dwivedi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
663 of 2023 at Police Station-Faridpur, District-Bareilly under Sections 354ka, 354kha, 376/511,
506, 452 IPC.
The applicant is in jail since 02.12.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 22.12.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Ashish Dwivedi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Ashish Ojha, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
Kala vs State Of U.P. on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64199135/
1
1. The victim and the applicant were intimate and had a consensual physical relationship.
2. The F.I.R. is the result of the said relationship going awry.

3. The victim has not made any allegation of commission of rape or forceful assault by the applicant in the F.I.R. lodged by her or in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
4.

Subsequently, false and aggravated allegations have been made by the victim against the applicant in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents only to save the failing prosecution case.

5. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C.
and Section 164 Cr.P.C., as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
6. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
7. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
8. The applicant has explained his criminal history.

It is also contended that the applicant has become a soft target and a convenient scapegoat for the police authorities who nominated him in a number of false cases to burnish their professional credentials.
The said cases do not have any bearing on the instant bail application.
9. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Kala be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
Kala vs State Of U.P. on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64199135/
2
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 15.4.2024 Dhananjai  Kala vs State Of U.P. on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64199135/
3
